- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon after a spike; reduce first 5–7 days’ forecast by 0.5–1.5%.
- Model underestimates late in the 30-day horizon after a strong upward move; increase last 5–7 days’ forecast by 0.5–1.5%.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33), model often fails to correct; apply mean reversion to last 3–5 days’ forecast.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment momentum in the 10–15 day window; if sentiment is trending, adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction over 3–5 days.
